lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A conference where the first session starts over breakfast. Snowflake Data-for-Breakfast was a morning on the cloud data platform, and Antoine went to hear how teams really run it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So not a product demo, more real stories?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. He went with some SQL under his belt from coursework and side projects, and wanted production stories. Infostrux gave a keynote that tied the morning together. The opening deck framed Snowflake as governed sharing first, speed second.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Think of a library that lends out single chapters instead of whole books. Partners can query the data they're allowed to see, and nothing else. That framing fits an organization whose first worry is which tables it can expose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One healthcare customer ran secure operations across three continents, sharing data with partners while keeping replication and governance in step. The lessons were that compliance goes hand in hand with sharing live data, that clinical operations need low latency and not just overnight batches, and that legal and technical sharing contracts travel together.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A tax-sector team landing very large datasets and exploring them without knowing every question in advance. Using Snowflake as a single layer to consolidate and transform data sped up troubleshooting and made lineage easier to explain to auditors. And analysts stopped emailing CSV files around.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The third one was about clean rooms?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. A clean room lets two companies compare overlapping datasets without pouring everything into one bucket. It's perfect for due diligence, where each side wants answers but doesn't want to hand over its raw data.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did he sum it up in a table?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He did. A central warehouse suits many teams with shared dimensions. Data sharing suits partners who need live slices. A clean room suits sensitive overlap analysis. Scaled-up compute suits exploratory spikes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Clearer vocabulary: clean room, share, row access policy. Useful in customer conversations even when Snowflake isn't part of the daily stack.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A nice snapshot of where Snowflake pushes: scale, sharing and governed collaboration. The full write-up has the tables and the lessons.
